STAGE: scoping the curvature-only round against the recorded failures.
GOAL: pick a coupling position that (a) keeps assignment and reconstruction on ONE set of codeword positions, (b) lets curvature enter in the SAME chart as a per-code geometric quantity, (c) lets the behaviour signal enter per (item,code) pair.
READ: task brief + the three earlier round summaries in the prompt (holonomy-path-behaviour-rq collapse: level2_distinct_prefixes=1, l3_collision=1.0, refinement_gain_bits=0, cosine loss blow-up 3.7e13, signed squared-difference fixes all degenerate once the residual is transported); the round brief's explicit ban on moving the residual into another chart (Lorentz/hyperboloid) before comparing with the ball codebook, and the note that a row-wise positive scalar cannot move an argmin.
OBSERVED/CONCLUDED: transport-based curvature (parallel transport, holonomy, cosine on transported residuals) is the proven failure family; it fails structurally because assignment reads transported codes while reconstruction reads untransported ones. Any new proposal must therefore leave every code and every residual in one Euclidean coordinate system, and must make curvature a scalar/weighted quantity attached to each individual codeword (its own radius inside the level's own ball, i.e. the Poincare conformal factor), while the behaviour signal must enter as a direction (per item, per codeword), not as a row constant.
DESIGN CHOSEN: per-item transition-direction anisotropy of the assignment metric, gated by the per-codeword Poincare conformal weight (1 - z_k^2), z_k = ||c_k|| / max_j ||c_j||, all inside R^d. Distance d_{i,k} = ||r - c_k||^2 + lambda_k * <r - c_k, u_i>^2 with lambda_k = 1 - min(z_k^2, 1-1/K). Behaviour-off sets u_i = 0 (Euclidean k-means), geometry-off sets lambda_k = 1 (behaviour-weighted, no curvature), both-on is the coupled metric. No new tuned constant: lambda is fully determined by codebook radii and the cap 1/K.
OPEN: nothing blocking; the final answer block is appended next.

FINAL ANSWER (complete idea block, curvature-only round).

IDEA: geoflow-metric-rq
TITLE: Behaviour-direction anisotropic assignment metric gated by the per-codeword Poincare conformal weight (one chart, one codebook)
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are chosen by plain Euclidean nearest-neighbour, so the quantisation error of an item is spread isotropically and the prefix that the generative recommender must predict carries no information about where the item's future actually lies. The previous round showed that trying to fix this by transporting residuals/codes between charts breaks assignment-versus-reconstruction consistency and collapses every level to one prefix. This idea keeps one chart and instead makes the residual-space metric itself direction-aware: error along the item's measured training transition direction is expensive at codewords that sit deep in the ball and cheap at codewords near the hyperbolic boundary, so the codeword that wins is the one whose quantisation error is placed where the next-step prediction does not need it.
NOVELTY: Not transport, not holonomy, not radial capacity allocation, not prefix ranking. Curvature appears only as the Poincare conformal factor of each individual codeword's own radial position inside the level's own ball (a per-code geometric scalar), and behaviour appears only as a per-(item,code) directional term <r - c_k, u_i>^2 built from directed training transitions. Assignment and reconstruction read the identical codeword positions; nothing is moved, mapped or re-embedded.
CHANGE: The argmin of every RQ level becomes argmin_k [ ||r - c_k||^2 + lambda_k * <r - c_k, u_i>^2 ] with u_i the unit mean latent displacement toward the item's training next-items and lambda_k = 1 - min((||c_k||/max_j||c_j||)^2, 1 - 1/K); z_q and the decoder loss keep using the same c_k, so reconstruction and assignment can never disagree.
SPECIFICATION: Per epoch, from training sequences only, build row-normalised transition weights w_ij = n_ij / sum_j n_ij over directed next-item counts; with detached item embeddings e_i, set u_i = sum_j w_ij (e_j - e_i), uhat_i = u_i / max(||u_i||, 1e-8), uhat_i = 0 if the item has no outgoing training transition. For each level l: z_k = ||c_{l,k}|| / max_j ||c_{l,j}||, s_k = 1 - min(z_k^2, 1 - 1/K), lambda_k = s_k (bounded in [1/K, 1], no tuned constant). For item i with residual r: proj_k = <r, uhat_i> - (C_l uhat_i)_k; d_k = ||r - c_k||^2 + lambda_k * proj_k^2; k* = argmin_k d_k; r <- r - c_{l,k*}; z_q = sum_l c_{l,k*_l}. Codebook updates, commitment loss, decoder, collision-extension token and Stage3 protocol are unchanged.
COST: One extra K x d matvec per (item, level) in the quantiser, i.e. about 3 * 1023 * K * d MACs per step at the frozen scale (24556 training items / 24 steps = ~1023 latents per step), the same order as the distance matmul already computed, so roughly +2-5 percent per step and no extra epoch. One epoch-level refresh of uhat costs ~(number of training transitions) * d MACs (~3e7), negligible. Total wall clock ~1.0-1.05x the baseline 3000-epoch Stage 2 run; no extra memory beyond a 1023 x K temporary and one d-vector per item.
HYPOTHESIS: If the prefix of an item should encode its behavioural future, then distorting the assignment metric along the measured transition direction must change which codeword wins for a substantial fraction of items and must raise Stage3 test_recall@10 above the 0.0555 baseline toward 0.065. Observables that must move: the frac

tion of (item, level-1) assignments that differ from the Euclidean argmin in the same run (should be clearly non-zero, expected 5-30 percent), the training-only prefix-transition lift P(prefix1(j)=prefix1(i) | i->j) / prior, and level-wise distinct prefix counts must stay > 1 with l3_collision well below 1.0.
RISKS: The anisotropy vanishes if neighbour latents are nearly identical (u_i ~ 0) or if most items are cold, reducing the run to the Euclidean baseline; the direction estimate from the embedding table can be dominated by popularity and rotate u_i toward a global mean direction, in which case the metric acts like a weak rank-1 shrinkage; boundary codewords could attract too many items and re-collapse prefixes (monitored, not tuned); and a single run cannot separate the recall gain from seed noise, so the effect has to be large enough to clear the baseline by more than the historical spread.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed first-order item-to-item transitions (sequential co-consumption), entering per (item, codeword) as a direction in latent space.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the Stage-2 training interaction split only, count n_ij = number of times item j occurs as the next item after item i in a training sequence; row-normalise to w_ij; with the currently trained (detached) item embedding table E, u_i = sum_j w_ij (e_j - e_i); normalise to unit length; zero vector if item i has no outgoing training transition. Recomputed once at the start of every epoch from the frozen transition counts, cached and detached, so it never back-propagates.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: Transition counts are built only from training-split sequences; validation and test interactions are never read when uhat is computed, and uhat is frozen before any evaluation or SID dump. No validation statistic (no recall, no entropy, no collision count) enters lambda, uhat, the cap 1/K or the codebook, so SID construction is a pure function of training interactions plus training-time parameters.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare-ball conformal factor with fixed negative curvature (-kappa, kappa=1 after unit normalisation of the level's codeword radii): gamma(c_k) proportional to 1/(1 - z_k^2) with z_k = ||c_k|| / max_j ||c_j||; the induced per-codeword weight s_k = 1 - min(z_k^2, 1 - 1/K) is the curvature-dependent metric scale at that codeword.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the RQ assignment step of every level, as the per-codeword multiplier of the directional quantisation error; it acts during training and is also used when SIDs are dumped, so the same geometry decides both.
COUPLING PATH: The single argmin that selects codeword k* for item i at level l. Removing the behaviour signal (uhat_i = 0) zeroes the directional term and leaves plain Euclidean k-means; removing the curvature (s_k = 1) removes the per-codeword gate and leaves behaviour-only isotropic weighting that cannot spread codewords radially. Both terms multiply the same scalar quantity inside the same distance, so neither is decorative.
COUPLING EQUATION: d_{i,l,k} = ||r_{i,l} - c_{l,k}||^2 + s_k * <r_{i,l} - c_{l,k}, uhat_i>^2, with s_k = 1 - min((||c_{l,k}|| / max_j ||c_{l,j}||)^2, 1 - 1/K) the Poincare conformal (curvature) term and <., uhat_i> the directed-transition (behaviour) term; k* = argmin_k d.
OBSERVABLES: (1) Stage3 test_recall@10 (target > 0.065 against the 0.0555 baseline); (2) fraction of level-1 assignments that differ from the Euclidean argmin computed on the same residual and codebook; (3) level-wise distin

ct prefix counts and l3_collision / l3_refinement_gain_bits, which must stay away from the previous round's collapse values; (4) training-only prefix-transition lift P(prefix1(j)=prefix1(i) | i->j) relative to the prefix prior; (5) distribution of s_k-weighted winning codeword radii, to see whether items actually spread radially.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: uhat_i set to the zero vector for all items (behaviour term inactive), curvature weights s_k kept at their computed values; the metric reduces to Euclidean squared distance because the directional term is identically zero, i.e. the baseline quantiser inside the same code. Not trained in this round, only present as a switch.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: s_k forced to 1 for all codewords (Euclidean, curvature-free direction weighting), uhat_i kept; the metric is behaviour-weighted but flat, with no per-codeword radial gate. Not trained in this round, only present as a switch.
ABLATION BOTH ON: The full coupled metric d = ||r - c_k||^2 + s_k * <r - c_k, uhat_i>^2 that the single scheduled 3000-epoch Stage 2 run and the frozen Stage 3 protocol actually use; the only arm that is trained.
SPEC EQUATIONS: Inputs per level l: codebook C_l in R^{K x d}, residuals r_i in R^d, unit (or zero) vectors uhat_i.
  z_k = ||c_{l,k}||_2 / max_j ||c_{l,j}||_2
  s_k = 1 - min(z_k^2, 1 - 1/K)
  a_i = <r_i, uhat_i>                       (scalar)
  b_ik = <c_{l,k}, uhat_i>   = (C_l uhat_i)_k
  d_ik = ||r_i - c_{l,k}||^2 + s_k * (a_i - b_ik)^2
  k*_i = argmin_k d_ik                      (ties: lowest index, deterministic)
  r_i <- r_i - c_{l,k*_i}
  z_q,i = sum_{l=1..3} c_{l,k*_{i,l}} , then the unchanged collision-extension token and decoder.
  Behaviour: w_ij = n_ij / sum_j n_ij ; u_i = sum_j w_ij (e_j - e_i) ; uhat_i = u_i / max(||u_i||, eps) or 0 if deg_out(i)=0.
  Switches: BEH_OFF -> uhat_i := 0 ; GEO_OFF -> s_k := 1 ; BOTH_ON -> above.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Input: the level's codeword matrix C_l (K x d, trainable), item residuals r_i (d), per-item unit behaviour direction uhat_i (d, detached, cached per epoch), curvature check kappa=1 and the derived cap 1/K. Output: integer codeword index k* per item per level used both to build z_q for the decoder and to define the SID prefix, plus the scalar per-codeword weights s_k and per-pair directional errors (a_i - b_ik)^2 logged for diagnostics. Nothing else in the quantiser, the codebook update, the loss or the collision handling changes.
SAFEGUARDS: uhat_i is L2-normalised with a 1e-8 floor and set to exactly zero for items without training transitions, so cold items fall back to Euclidean quantisation; z_k is clamped to <= 1 - 1/K so s_k stays in [1/K, 1] and can never be zero or negative; the max-norm denominator uses the current codebook with a 1e-12 floor for an all-zero codebook; degenerate equal norms keep all s_k equal, which is exactly the geometry-off behaviour; neighbour displacements are computed under no_grad from detach()ed embeddings so behaviour cannot back-propagate and cannot blow up the graph; the directional term is a square, so the sign of uhat is irrelevant and no cosine division by a small residual norm is taken (the previous round's 3.7e13 blow-up cannot recur); assignment ties are broken by lowest index for determinism at SID-dump time; K and 1/K are structural (number of codewords), not tuned constants; diagnostics (distinct prefixes, collision, usage share) are logged after each epoch for monitoring only and never abort or alter training.
END
